newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Eskom intl local currency BBB.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Eskom intl local currency BBB.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agnecy, said on Wednesday it has assigned an interantional local currency rating of BBB to South Africa's Eskom.
"Tangible governmental support is restricted to State guarantees of the majority of the 22 percent of gross borrowings at year end 1995 denominated in foreign currencies," IBCA said in a statement.

"As part of Eskom's contribution to the restructuring of South Africa, the utility has built up provisions of 1.2 billion Rand with regard to municipal authorities unable to meet debts to the utility as a result of rent and service boycotts throughout the country."

The agency added that following the impending formalisation of State ownership, Eskom will return to a position where both direct corporate taxation and, potentially, dividend payments will become payable.
"Reorganisation of the utility may also see the integrated structure split into separate generation, transmission and distribution operations," it said.
Eskom had traditionally shared responsibility for the latter with local municipalities, but has now assumed a greater role in retail distribution, IBCA added.
IBCA said it believed it was unlikely that Eskom would be privatised until such time as substantial progress has been made in increasing the number of households supplied with power.

"Despite Eskom's commitment to reducing the real price of power by 20 percent over the seven years to 1998 (for which it remains on target), productivity gains and effective debt management have contributed to steady improvements to its financial position," the agency said.
"Net gearing of 140 percent is anticipated to reach the international benchmark of 100 percent by the turn of the century."
The rating firm added that despite greater regulation, and higher levels of cross-subsidisation, Eskom continues to improve debt and coverage ratios.
